classification.difficultyReason: Divide the stock into groups of six and interpret the final quotient and remainder as complete packages and leftover cans.

content.prompt: Cans of lemonade are to be packaged together in groups of 6. The factory has 4567 cans to be packaged. How many packages of 6 cans are there and how many are left over?

answer.short: 761 packages of 6 cans, with 1 can left over.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{array}{r}\hphantom{000}\hspace{0.9em}\underline{\hphantom{0}\hspace{0.9em}\hphantom{0}\mathllap{7}\hspace{0.9em}\hphantom{0}\mathllap{6}\hspace{0.9em}\hphantom{0}\mathllap{1}\hspace{0.9em}}\\
\hphantom{000}\mathllap{6\big)}\hspace{0.9em}\hphantom{0}\mathllap{4}\hspace{0.9em}\hphantom{0}\mathllap{5}\hspace{0.9em}\hphantom{0}\mathllap{{}^{3}6}\hspace{0.9em}\hphantom{0}\mathllap{7}\hspace{0.9em}\end{array}\quad\text{remainder }1$$
$$4567\div6=761\text{ remainder }1$$
There are 761 packages of 6 cans, with 1 can left over.
